claims.text: Replacing fixed-form EAM references with a machine-learning potential trained on solid and liquid ab initio configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The ML reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 30–50% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
The proposed method applies to high-entropy alloys containing five or more components, represented by equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed applicable temperature range is approximately 0.9–1.0 Tm.
Local descriptors such as SOAP or bispectrum components enable the ML potential to capture many-body correlations and local atomic environments.
Capturing many-body correlations and local environments bridges the diversity of ab initio configurations and the simplified reference model.
Training on an expanded and iteratively generated set of high-temperature solid and liquid ab initio snapshots will improve representation of subtle energy variations.
Training on those snapshots will improve representation of subtle force variations.
Improved representation of energy and force variations will reduce mismatch along the free-energy integration path.
The ML potential will reproduce the ab initio potential-energy landscape more faithfully than the EAM reference.
The proposed method will produce free-energy calculations with uncertainties below 10 meV/atom.
Reducing integration-path mismatch will improve predictions of melting properties.
TOR-TILD fixed-form EAM potentials have limited ability to capture many-body behavior and high-temperature disordered configurations.
The approach will be most effective for high-entropy alloys close to their melting points.
Insufficient configurational coverage in the training set could limit the predicted improvements.
Failure to converge within 10 meV/atom of an ab initio benchmark or experimental melting free energy is stipulated to falsify the hypothesis.
